column1: # Packages governed by the protocol's own platform qualification.
# When the SUPPLIED conformance root publishes
# `vectors/conformance-claim-v3-qualification.json`, that vector -- not this
# file -- decides which platforms are excluded. This table then only says which
# packages the exclusion reaches, and which case must still run and pass there
# to prove the exclusion is real fail-closed behaviour rather than a quiet
# omission.
# `default_excluded_on` is the fallback for a SUPPLIED root that predates the
# vector (e.g. an older CURATOR_CONFORMANCE_ROOT passed explicitly). The
# committed conformance pin is NOT such a root: it publishes
# `vectors/conformance-claim-v3-qualification.json`, so on the default lane the
# vector is authoritative and this fallback stays dormant. Without it, a
# pre-vector root would lose an exclusion that is a property of the
# implementation rather than of the root.
# `internal/godriver` implements rc5-native-control-inventory-v1, which defines
# control records for macOS and Windows only, so linux is excluded under any
# root; the rc.5 vector states the same thing normatively, with
# `until_task: TASK-260728-1skseh`. A root that publishes the vector always
# wins, so the fallback can never contradict a live protocol statement, and
# when the vector stops excluding a platform the package returns to the full
# run there automatically.
# The exclusion is never taken on trust. The assertion case drives
# `probeNativeControlsFor("")` and `probeNativeControlsFor("linux")` and
# requires `build_execution_control_unavailable` from both -- the manager
# refuses BEFORE any worker starts. It is pure and compiles everywhere, so the
# excluded runner still proves the boundary it is excluded by.
# Columns are TAB separated:
#   package  assertion_case  default_excluded_on  note
# package
internal/godriver
column4: an uncovered inventory platform is refused before the worker starts
